item.title: 165-million-year-old fossil from China reveals mammal ancestor that swam and swallowed like mammals
item.description: Scientists have identified a 165-million-year-old mammal predecessor from China that had a broad tail for swimming and throat bones similar to those of modern mammals. Named Megacauda sungei, the Jurassic-era animal could chew and swallow food using specialised structures. Published in Nature, the findings offer new insights into how early mammals developed different feeding abilities.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Inside Luke Bryan’s 150-acre Tennessee farm with a rescue barn
item.description: Luke Bryan and his wife, Caroline Boyer, purchased a 150-acre farm in Williamson County, Tennessee, in 2012. They transformed it into Red Bird Farm, featuring a 10,000-square-foot main house, a guesthouse, and a party barn. The couple built a bass lake, which was a significant part of Bryan's childhood dream. Their farm also functions as a rescue space for animals under the Brett Boyer Foundation.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Queens’ historic Lost Battalion Hall reopens after $25.9m reconstruction
item.description: Queens’ historic Lost Battalion Hall has reopened after a $25.9 million reconstruction. The 87-year-old recreation center now has upgraded fitness rooms, accessible facilities, modern safety systems and a refreshed basketball court.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Dr Phil lists Beverly Hills estate for $67.5m after buying it for $29.8m
item.description: Dr. Phil McGraw and his wife Robin have put their luxurious Beverly Hills estate on the market for an impressive $67.5 million. After acquiring it for $29.8 million in 2010 and taking another seven years to complete its construction by 2011, the sprawling 16,079 square foot residence is accompanied by guest and staff quarters. Among its exquisite features are a swimming pool, wine cellar, and tennis court.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Listed at $8M, this 112-year-old home sells for $15M
item.description: At 2 Sixth Avenue in San Francisco, a remarkable house came onto the market with an asking price of $7.999 million but ultimately sold for a staggering $15 million. Having belonged to one family for seven decades, the well-appointed home includes four bedrooms and three bathrooms across 4,490 square feet.

item.title: Wisconsin protects over 1,700 Lake Superior acres, restores wetlands and habitat
item.description: Wisconsin's Lake Superior shoreline has witnessed a transformative conservation effort, safeguarding over 1,700 acres through collaboration between the US Fish and Wildlife Service and Landmark Conservancy. By utilizing conservation easements, the project enabled landowners to retain property rights while preserving vital habitats. Key activities included the planting of conifers and the management of invasive species, fulfilling the environmental aspirations of the Great Lakes Restoration Initiative.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Third school attack in Poland in a week sparks safety concerns
item.description: Three school attacks recently occurred in Poland, resulting in injuries to multiple individuals. The first attack involved a 19-year-old student injuring nine people at a vocational school. A second incident by a 15-year-old resulted in the death of a custodian and injuries to others. Authorities responded by tightening security measures across various schools and detaining several individuals for potential threats.
item.dc:creator: Mahima Sharma

item.title: Scotty’s Castle reopens for limited tours 11 years after Death Valley flash flood forced its closure
item.description: More than a decade after a flash flood forced Scotty’s Castle to close, Death Valley National Park is bringing visitors back for limited exterior tours from October 10 as a $71 million restoration effort continues.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: This California mansion has a train, tunnel and station
item.description: A luxurious estate in La Cañada Flintridge was recently sold for $8.5 million, attracting numerous potential buyers. The property includes a custom five-passenger garden railway that enhances its unique appeal and charm. Additionally, the house consists of six bedrooms, eight bathrooms, and a gourmet kitchen perfect for entertaining. Extensive outdoor features include a swimming pool, vegetable garden, and manicured landscapes recognized with multiple awards.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Restoration Ecology Study Findings: Tidal flows fuel Marsh Wren surge; broader marsh birds gain
item.description: California's initiative to revive the Dutch Slough wetlands has led to a stunning resurgence of Marsh Wren numbers. Recent bird surveys from 2020 to 2025 indicate significant increases in the density of various marsh-dwelling species. This restoration process involved planting indigenous plants and reinstating tidal flows to previous agricultural terrains. While some species saw a decline, overall avian diversity thrived in these rejuvenated areas.

item.title: In 1969, a Nevada man built a desert home from junk; today, Thunder Mountain is a free attraction
item.description: Thunder Mountain Monument in Nevada features sculptures created from discarded materials by Frank Van Zant. This unique roadside attraction developed from his personal vision to honor Native American history. After a fire in 1983, the site faced preservation challenges until it was recognized as a historic site in 1992. The monument is maintained today with visitor donations and a caretaker's assistance.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: David Gilmour sold his guitars for $21.5 million to fund climate change and nature protection work
item.description: In June 2019, David Gilmour sold over 120 guitars, significantly benefitting ClientEarth with the proceeds. Among them was the iconic 1969 Fender Stratocaster, which achieved a record sale price. These funds were dedicated to advancing environmental law initiatives aimed at combatting climate change. This remarkable auction intertwined rock legacy and ecological activism, illustrating Gilmour's commitment to fostering a sustainable future through music.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Rihanna’s foundation teamed up with bicycle company to help girls in Malawi get to school
item.description: In an inspiring collaboration, Rihanna's Clara Lionel Foundation has teamed up with Ofo to enhance educational access for girls in Malawi through the 1 KM Action initiative. This initiative not only provides bicycles but also offers scholarships, alleviating the burdens of travel and educational expenses. Following the partnership announcement, the first bicycles arrived, significantly facilitating school attendance.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Jamie Oliver’s cooking programme began in 2008; by 2024, his food education work had reached 115,000+ people
item.description: Jamie Oliver's Ministry of Food, established in 2008, has made significant strides in promoting culinary skills across communities. By March 2024, it successfully engaged over 115,000 participants through school and community-based initiatives. The program not only focuses on delivering practical cooking techniques but also aims at fostering healthier dietary choices for families.
